grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Chinese has no he/she difference in speech: tā sounds the same. The plural ending 们 (men) makes a group of people.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Nouns do not change for plural. Use a number and a measure word, or just the context.

grammar.title: 是: to be
text: Use 是 (shì) between two nouns: A 是 B. Do not use 是 before an adjective.

grammar.title: Verbs do not change
text: Chinese verbs never change their form. Time words or small particles show the time.
ex: tomorrow I will go to Beijing
we watch TV in the evening

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Word order is Subject, Verb, Object, like English. Time and place come before the verb.

grammar.title: Negation
text: Use 不 (bù) before most verbs and adjectives. Use 没 (méi) for 有 and for the past. Say 不 as bú before a fourth tone.
rows: 我 不 喝 茶
ex: I do not have a car
I do not want to go
tā méi gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Add 吗 (ma) to the end of a statement to make a yes-no question. Or use the verb pattern: verb + 不 + verb.
rows: 你 是 学生 吗
你 去 不 去

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words stay in the same place as the answer. You do not move them to the front.

grammar.title: Particles
text: Small words at the end or after a word give the grammar. They have no meaning of their own.
ex: wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū

grammar.title: This, that, which
text: Put a measure word after 这, 那 and 哪 when you point at a thing: 这个, 那个, 哪个.
ex: zhè běn shū shì wǒ de
nà gè rén shì wǒ de lǎoshī

grammar.title: Adjectives
text: Adjectives work like verbs. Do not use 是. Put 很 (very) in front, even when you only mean "is".

grammar.title: Wanting and asking
text: 想 means "would like to" and 要 means "want to, will". For polite asking, begin with 请 or 请问.
ex: I would like to go to China
excuse me, where is the toilet?

grammar.title: Existing and having
text: 有 means "have" and also "there is". 没有 is the opposite. 在 tells you where something is.
rows: 桌子 上 有 书
书 在 桌子 上
ex: I do not have a brother

grammar.title: Measure words
text: Between a number and a noun you need a measure word. 个 (ge) works for most things.

grammar.title: Formal and informal
text: Use 您 (nín) for one older or respected person. Use 你 with friends. 请 makes any request polite.

grammar.title: Commands
text: A command is just the verb. Use 请 to be polite and 别 or 不要 to say "do not".

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: These helper verbs go before the main verb. 会 is "can" by learning, 能 is "can" by ability or chance, 可以 is "may".

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: 在 (zài) is "at, in, on". Use place words like 上 (on), 里 (in), 下 (under) after the noun.
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the chair
the school is next to the park

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Use 比 (bǐ) to compare: A 比 B + adjective. Use 最 (zuì) for "the most".
rows: 他 比 我 高
我 没有 他 高
ex: this one is cheaper than that one
I am not as tall as him

grammar.title: Past, now and future
text: Add 了 for a finished action, 过 for "have ever", 在 for "is doing", and 会 or 要 for the future.
ex: the train is about to leave

grammar.title: Everyday sentences
text: Short sentences you can use every day.
ex: I go to work by bus
I watch TV in the evening
I go to bed at eleven

grammar.title: 把 sentences (bǎ)
text: 把 moves the object in front of the verb to show what is done to it. The verb must have something after it: a result, a place or 了. Use it when the object is known and you stress what happens to it.
rows: Negative: 没 goes before 把
ex: wǒ bǎ zuòyè zuò wán le
he put the book on the table
tā bǎ shū fàngzài zhuōzi shàng
I left my wallet at home
wǒ bǎ qiánbāo wàng zài jiālǐ le
she has not tidied the room
tā hái méi bǎ fángjiān zhěnglǐ hǎo

grammar.title: 被 passive sentences (bèi)
text: 被 marks the doer after the receiver: receiver 被 doer + verb + result. The doer can be left out. Mostly used for events with a bad or unwanted result, but not only.
rows: wǒ de zìxíngchē bèi tōu le
Negative: 没 goes before 被
ex: wǒ de zìxíngchē bèi tōu le
the cup was broken by him
he was criticised by the teacher
the window was blown open by the wind
the problem has not been solved
I was invited to the party

grammar.title: Result complements
text: A second verb or adjective after the verb tells the result: 听懂 (hear and so understand), 看见 (look and so see). Negative uses 没, not 不. Add 得 or 不 in the middle for can / cannot: 听得懂 / 听不懂.
rows: 听懂 · 听得懂 · 听不懂
ex: I cannot understand what he says
wǒ tīngbùdǒng tā shuō de huà

grammar.title: Directional complements
text: 来 and 去 after a verb show direction toward or away from the speaker. They can follow 上, 下, 进, 出, 回, 过, 起: 走进来, 拿出去, 跑回来. A place goes between the two parts: 走进教室来.
rows: shànglái xiàlai jìnlái chūlái huílai guòlái
上来 下来 进来 出来 回来 过来
shàngqù xiàqù jìnqù chūqù huíqu guòqù
上去 下去 进去 出去 回去 过去
ex: the teacher walked into the classroom

grammar.title: 得 complements: how well
text: To say how well or how fast something is done, repeat the verb if there is an object, then add 得 and an adjective: 他说汉语说得很好. With no object: 她跑得很快. Negative: 说得不好.
rows: shuō hànyǔ shuō de hěn hǎo
ex: tā shuō hànyǔ shuō de hěn hǎo

grammar.title: 越来越 and 越…越…
text: 越来越 + adjective: more and more, something keeps changing. 越…越…: the more A, the more B. Both go before the verb or adjective.
ex: it is getting colder and colder
he is getting taller and taller
the more I study, the more interesting it is
the more he talks, the happier he gets
cities are getting bigger and bigger

grammar.title: Linking sentences: 虽然…但是 and friends
text: Chinese sentences usually keep the connecting words in pairs. 虽然 and 但是 are both used (unlike English although ... but). 因为 and 所以 are also both used. The condition or reason comes first.
ex: although it is cold, he still goes running
suīrán tiānqì hěn lěng dànshì tā háishi qù pǎobù le
虽然天气很冷,但是他还是去跑步了
because I was ill, I did not go to school
yīnwèi wǒ shēngbìng le suǒyǐ méi qù shàngxué
因为我生病了,所以没去上学
if it rains tomorrow, we will not go
rúguǒ míngtiān xiàyǔ wǒmen jiù bù qù le
如果明天下雨,我们就不去了
as long as you work hard, you can succeed
zhǐyào nǐ nǔlì jiù néng chénggōng
she is not only clever but also kind
tā bùdàn cōngming érqiě hěn shànliáng
她不但聪明,而且很善良
even if it is difficult, I will not give up
jíshǐ hěn kùnnan wǒ yě búhuì fàngqì
即使很困难,我也不会放弃

grammar.title: 是…的: stressing how, when, where
text: When an action is already finished and you want to ask or tell how, when, where or with whom, wrap the detail in 是…的. 是 can be dropped in speech; 的 stays. Negative: 不是…的.
rows: nǐ shì zài nǎr xué de hànyǔ
wǒ shì zuò fēijī lái de
ex: nǐ shì zài nǎr xué de hànyǔ
wǒ shì zuò fēijī lái de
zhè běnshū shì shuí xiě de
wǒmen shì zài běijīng rènshi de
I did not come by car

grammar.title: 连…都 and 除了…以外
text: 连 + noun + 都/也 means even: 连饭都没吃 (did not even eat). 除了…以外 means apart from, and the rest depends on 还 (as well) or 都 (all the others).
ex: tā lián fàn dōu méi chī
I do not know a single character
wǒ lián yígè zì yě bù rènshi
chúle tā yǐwài dàjiā dōu lái le
除了他以外,大家都来了
apart from Chinese I also study English
chúle hànyǔ wǒ hái xué yīngyǔ
she even forgot her own birthday
tā lián zìjǐ de shēngrì dōu wàng le
她连自己的生日都忘了
apart from Sunday I am busy every day
chúle xīngqītiān yǐwài wǒ tiāntiān dōu hěn máng
除了星期天以外,我天天都很忙

grammar.title: 一边…一边…, 一…就…, 先…然后…
text: 一边…一边… : two actions at the same time. 一…就… : as soon as A, B. 先…然后… / 先…再… : first A, then B.
ex: 我一边吃饭一边看电视
he goes home as soon as class ends
first wash your hands, then eat
I fall asleep the moment I lie down
wǒ yī tǎng xià jiù shuìzháo le

sounds.intro: Chinese is written in pinyin, the Latin spelling of the sounds, with four tones. The tone changes the meaning, so learn it with every word.
rows: high and flat, like holding a note
like the p, t, k in "spin": no puff of air
bā 八, dà 大, gē 歌
like English p, t, k with a strong puff of air
pà 怕, tā 他, kě 渴
like English (h is a little rougher)
mā 妈, nǐ 你, fā 发, lái 来, hǎo 好
like "j" in "jeep", with the tongue flat and the lips smiling
like "ch" in "cheese", with a puff of air, lips smiling
like "j" in "jam", with the tongue curled back
like "ch" in "church", tongue curled back, with a puff
like English y and w (they are spellings of i and u)
ee, like "see"; after z, c, s, zh, ch, sh, r it is a short buzz
nǐ 你, sì 四, shí 十
say "ee" with rounded lips, like French "u"
huì 会, liù 六, wèn 问
notes: Do not read pinyin like English: q is not "kw", x is not "ks", c is "ts" and zh is like "j".
When a 3rd tone comes before another 3rd tone, the first one is said as a 2nd tone: nǐ hǎo is said "ní hǎo". The spelling stays the same.
不 (bù) changes to bú before a 4th tone: bú shì. 一 (yī) is said yí before a 4th tone and yì before the others.
In pinyin, words are written together, and names start with a capital letter.
